t:
(a) In General.—Section 114(b)(1)(I) of title 4, United States Code, is amended—
        (1) by inserting “(or any plan, program, or arrangement that is in writing, that provides for retirement payments in recognition of prior service to be made to a retired partner, and that is in effect immediately before retirement begins)” after “section 3121(v)(2)(C) of such Code”, 
        (2) by inserting “which may include income described in subparagraphs (A) through (H)” after “(not less frequently than annually”, 
        (3) by adding at the end the following:“The fact that payments may be adjusted from time to time pursuant to such plan, program, or arrangement to limit total disbursements under a predetermined formula, or to provide cost of living or similar adjustments, will not cause the periodic payments provided under such plan, program, or arrangement to fail the ‘substantially equal periodic payments’ test.”, and 
        (4) by adding at the end the following:“(4) For purposes of this section, the term ‘retired partner’ is an individual who is described as a partner in section 7701(a)(2) of the Internal Revenue Code of 1986 and who is retired under such individual’s partnership agreement.”.  
    (b) Application.—The amendments made by this section apply to amounts received after December 31, 1995.

fable.w: This section only amends the definition of retirement income in 4 U.S.C. 114 (retired partner plans, the periodic payments test) and sets an effective date. The tempting reading is that the words "partnership agreement" or "plan, program, or arrangement" signal outside involvement, but these describe private retirement arrangements, not consultation with anyone on a federal decision. There is no comment period, hearing, advisory body, rulemaking, consultation with outside parties, or right to sue.
fable.s: The amendments made by this section apply to amounts received after December 31, 1995.

qwen_block.w: This section amends the Internal Revenue Code regarding the definition of 'substantially equal periodic payments' for retired partners. It defines tax treatment and applicability dates but does not require consultation, public comment, hearings, or coordination with outside parties before a federal decision is made. The text is purely definitional and regulatory in nature.
qwen_block.s: Section 114(b)(1)(I) of title 4, United States Code, is amended

opus.w: This section changes the definition of retirement income covered by 4 U.S.C. 114 and defines 'retired partner'. It does not create any process for people outside the federal government to take part in a federal decision. 'Partnership agreement' and 'arrangement' are just definitional words, not a consultation, hearing, comment period, or advisory body, so the keyword reading fails.
opus.s: the term ‘retired partner’ is an individual who is described as a partner in section 7701(a)(2) of the Internal Revenue Code of 1986 and who is retired under such individual’s partnership agreement.
opus.b:
**Step 1: the tempting reading.** The section uses the words "arrangement" and "partnership agreement," which might look like some kind of formal process involving outside parties. That reading fails. These words only define which retirement payments count for the state income tax limits in 4 U.S.C. § 114. Nothing here has the federal government consulting outsiders, holding hearings, setting up an advisory body, requiring rulemaking, or granting a right to sue.

**Step 2: label.**

qwen_chat.w: This section amends the Internal Revenue Code to clarify the definition of 'substantially equal periodic payments' for tax purposes. It does not require or recommend any consultation, public comment, hearing, or advisory input from outside parties before a federal decision is made. The mention of 'partners' and 'retirement payments' refers to the subjects of the tax rule, not to participants in a decision-making process.
qwen_chat.s: Section 114(b)(1)(I) of title 4, United States Code, is amended... by adding at the end the following:“The fact that payments may be adjusted from time to time pursuant to such plan, program, or arrangement to limit total disbursements under a predetermined formula, or to provide cost of living or similar adjustments, will not cause the periodic payments provided under such plan, program, or arrangement to fail the ‘substantially equal periodic payments’ test.”
qwen_chat.b: Tempting-but-wrong reading: One might argue that because the text amends tax code provisions regarding "partners" and "retirement payments," it involves private individuals (partners) interacting with the government. However, this is merely a definitional amendment to the Internal Revenue Code to clarify what constitutes "substantially equal periodic payments" for tax purposes. It does not establish a process for consultation, comment, hearing, or advisory input from outside parties before a federal decision is made. It is a substantive rule change, not a procedural participation mechanism.
